newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN seeks probe into east Zaire massacre reports.
newsitem.headline: UN seeks probe into east Zaire massacre reports.

text.p: The outgoing U.N. human rights chief appealed to donors on Thursday to fund the deployment of observers to east Zaire to investigate reports of alleged massacres of Rwandan Hutu refugees by mainly Tutsi rebels.

A United Nations statement said Jose Ayala Lasso was deeply concerned by reports from Zairean human rights groups alleging the existence of mass graves in east Zaire, near camps which sheltered Rwandan Hutu refugees and were overrun by rebels late in 1996.
The Ecuadorian diplomat, who steps down on March 15 to
become his country's foreign minister, has asked the U.N.'s special human rights investigator for Zaire, Roberto Garreton, to investigate the massacre allegations, the statement said.
He was considering sending observers to Zaire, where the U.N. human rights office has only two observers in the capital Kinshasa, if donors provided funds, it added.

Zaire's main human rights group, the Association for the Defence of Human Rights in Zaire (Azadho), has alleged large-scale massacres by the rebels since they captured much of Zaire's North and South Kivu provinces last November.

Azadho, although a harsh critic of Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko whom the rebels are fighting to overthrow, has cited dates, places, witnesses and grave sites at Mugunga, Kibumba, and Katale camps to back charges against the rebels and their alleged Rwandan and Ugandan army backers.
Last week Belgium, the former colonial power in the region, said it was alarmed by reports of a "second genocide" in Zaire.
The U.N. refugee agency UNHCR says it has no confirmation of the alleged massacres of Rwandan Hutus.
More than half a million minority Tutsis and Hutu moderates died in Rwanda's 1994 genocide blamed on majority Hutus who then fled to east Zaire, setting the scene for the current conflict.
